content.comment_body: Hello, I need advice. I'm measuring temperature using four Pt100 sensors connected with two [product_name] modules. However, the device ([product_name]) will be installed about 15 meters away from the sensors. How do you think this distance impacts measurement accuracy? The [product_name] manual mentions a recommended cable length of 10 meters. Thanks in advance for any suggestions.

Hi [user_name], interesting question! One advantage of our PT100 module is that it supports 3-wire measurements. This setup lets the module estimate the resistance of the lead wires, which is useful for calculating the true temperature at the sensor tip. Unlike signal measurement with 0/4..20 mA, temperature is measured using the resistance of a platinum filament—100 ohms at 0.01 °C. Lead length, wire thickness, and local temperatures can affect resistance. Using 3 wires, the module corrects for lead resistance before relaying results to the [product_name] system. For 2-wire sensors, accuracy depends on wire quality and environment. The manual recommends 10 meters of shielded wire for best accuracy (as noted on page 263). With 15 meters, accuracy may decline by about 50%, e.g. from ±1.0% to ±1.5% for positive temperature ranges and even more in the negative range. A 3-wire setup greatly reduces this loss of accuracy. I hope this helps. You can find more information about temperature measurement principles online. (Background: experience in temperature and humidity calibration, standards, and measurement applications — always interesting to see these principles in use with [product_name].)

Hi [user_name], thanks for your response! It was really helpful. My sensors actually use 4 wires, so one wire isn't connected. Also, I've found your other forum answers very insightful. Wishing you a great day!

Hi [user_name], I use 3-wire Pt100 sensors with [product_name] daily for solar thermal systems and have run cable lengths of up to 40 meters without encountering issues. Based on my experience, even 100 meters should be possible without significant problems. The accuracy has been confirmed in many installed systems, including one with a wood-fired home heating system boiling water at 99.75–100.00°C from 30 meters away. The most important part is ensuring the shielded braid is continuous and properly connected to the PE [product_name] connector. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are discussing how cable length affects PT100 temperature sensor measurements using [product_name] modules. The main concern is possible accuracy loss beyond the manual's recommended 10 meters. Users provide practical advice and share experience using 3- and 4-wire configurations, with feedback that accurate readings are possible at greater cable lengths if shielding and wiring are correctly implemented. The conversation reflects confidence in the product's reliability but highlights the need for clearer guidelines on installations exceeding specified cable length.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to maintain accurate and reliable temperature measurements even when cable lengths exceed those specified in the manual, using standard PT100 sensors and [product_name] modules.
